verdicts.rewritten_summary: Korea Times (22 July 2024): the Seoul appellate court dismissed the state's appeal and finalised a 300,000 won damages award (against a 3 million won claim) ruling that police advice to a person transitioning from male to female, who had obtained court approval for a family-register gender change in 2020, to avoid women's public restrooms infringed personal rights; the appellate court held that comfortable restroom use is a fundamental and universal human right. The article also reports a 2021 NHRCK survey of 591 transgender respondents, 41% of whom reported avoiding facilities out of fear. This is the national framework this division is scored against; the article contains no North Gyeongsang-specific incident.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Yonhap wire (8 May 2024): a regional court in Yeongdong approved changing the registered sex from male to female for five transgender applicants without sex-reassignment surgery, holding that it is against the law to condition gender change on surgery, and that court guidelines requiring surgery are now mere reference, not criteria; the court said every human being has the right to form their character and live a life according to their gender identity. This national ruling removed the surgical prerequisite for registered-sex change and is the framework this division is scored against; the wire contains no North Gyeongsang-specific content.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Public Prosecutor's Office (Ministerio Público) news note of 23 March 2022 on its Observatory of Criminality study of intentional deaths of LGTB people in Peru 2012-2021: 84 criminal complaints involving 88 victims and 72 identified suspects; 58% of deaths concentrated in six fiscal districts - Lima (12), La Libertad (10), Lima Norte (10), Lima Este (7), Lima Sur (6) and Callao (6) - placing La Libertad second in absolute count (level with Lima Norte) behind Lima. The study was developed with the Justice Ministry human-rights office and the University Cayetano Heredia LGTB-rights observatory with UNDP support, and yielded recommendations including training criminal prosecutors on LGTB-victim identification and monitoring systems.
verdicts.note: national study with a La Libertad-specific datapoint; record-text claim (10 of 88, second absolute count) verified in cache

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Regional Government La Libertad norms page for Ordenanza Regional N.° 009-2024-GRLL-CR (6 September 2024): approves promoting labour inclusion of travesti, transsexual and transgender persons in the region, declaring that every such person has the right to formal, dignified and productive work in equitable and satisfactory conditions without discrimination on grounds of gender identity and/or its expression, and recognising the trans community as a group in a situation of vulnerability in La Libertad. The cached page carries only this normative header (title, date, operative sentence) with the full text linked as PDF; it directly evidences the record's claim that this regional council legislated for trans labour inclusion.
verdicts.note: region-specific ordinance source; cache is a brief header/operative-text page, full text in linked PDF and the El Peruano record

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Official-gazette record (El Peruano, publication date 07/11/2024) of Ordenanza Regional N.° 000009-2024-GRLL-CR, presented in the regional council's ordinary session of 3 September 2024, debated, approved and signed in Trujillo on 6 September 2024: Its object is positive-action measures for the effective labour inclusion of travesti, transsexual and transgender persons in La Libertad - the right to formal, dignified, productive work in equitable and satisfactory conditions. It cites constitutional equality guarantees and article 323 of the Penal Code (discrimination as a crime), recalls a 2014 regional-council session framework against discrimination on sexual orientation and gender identity, recommends local governments issue municipal ordinances recognising gender identity and fundamental rights, and orders a working group (mesa de trabajo); it enters into force the day after publication in El Peruano.
verdicts.note: superseded: batch freshness flagged this URL unknown/JS-rendered-unverified, but the cached copy is readable and confirms norm identity, dates and operative text - that unverifiability finding is superseded by the readable cache

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Wayka (27 May 2025): Marcia Paucara Cora, a 48-year-old trans woman, was found dead in a hostel room in Tacna on 19 April 2025, the autopsy recording death by mechanical asphyxia through compression of the airways, after entering the hostel with a man who registered under a false identity and left alone about two hours later; the case is being investigated as a possible hate crime - an offence motivated by prejudice and discrimination on grounds of the victim's sexual orientation or gender identity. Her family and local LGTBIQ+ collectives held a vigil on Friday 23 May demanding justice, describing the killing as the reflection of a structural system of violence that silences trans lives. Context offered: Peru has no gender-identity-recognition legislation and no law sanctioning hate crimes, and activists note a recently promulgated legislative proposal (congressman Alejandro Muñante) restricting access to public bathrooms by sexual orientation; the Public Prosecutor's Office identified 84 criminal complaints on LGTB deaths between January 2012 and May 2021 (most victims gay men 55.8%, trans women 36.4%).
verdicts.note: region-source (Tacna incident); confirms record-text date of 19 April 2025 and false-identity registration detail

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Trome (updated 21 May 2025): a 48-year-old trans woman was found dead inside the 'Los 5 Titos' hostel on Arias y Aragüez street in central Tacna after entering on a Sunday with a man who later left alone carrying a white bag; she was initially processed as NN until identified through the hostel's cameras; police were analysing surveillance footage inside and outside the hostel to trace the suspect's escape route; relatives denounced the crime and demanded police action. The body was discovered by hostel staff when the rental time expired; no suspect had been identified in the audited text.
verdicts.note: region-source (Tacna incident); news account without calendar date (record date of 19 April 2025 is sourced by the Wayka report)

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Publimetro Colombia (27 September 2026) on Caribe Afirmativo's 2025 report 'Un sistema que falla: prejuicio, violencia e impunidad contra personas LGBTIQ+ en Colombia': nationally 270 victims in 2025, a 63% increase over 2024 (165 homicides), one killing every 32 hours. For the Atlántico department it documents 54 intrafamily-violence cases, 41 sexual offences, 12 discrimination cases, 8 digital-violence cases, 69 threats, 2 killings of LGBTIQ+ human-rights defenders and 8 lethal-violence cases, and designates Barranquilla and Soledad as territories with 'high' threat levels for this population; it recalls the department's and Barranquilla's development plans commit coordinated action with the prosecutor's office, police and judiciary to strengthen reporting, investigation and prosecution of violence against LGBTIQ+ people. It also reports threats show near-total impunity, with 99.8% of cases never advancing past the investigation stage.
verdicts.note: region-specific source carrying the named escalation warning and Atlántico case counts; record-text figures (54/41/12/8/69/2/8, high-threat Barranquilla and Soledad, 99.8%) verified in cache

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Caribe Afirmativo's own 2025 report 'Un sistema que falla: prejuicio, violencia e impunidad contra personas LGBTIQ+ en Colombia': in 2025 one LGBTIQ+ person was killed every 32 hours, and violence runs a continuum from discrimination through intrafamily violence (1,531 cases), sexual violence (628 cases) and threats (1,184 victims) to homicide and impunity; the report documents territorial expansion of the violence, including towards territories with illegal-economy corridors and weak state presence, and criticises the insufficient state response. verdicts.rewritten_summary: El Tiempo data investigation (2025): Nawar Jiménez, a trans social leader who had campaigned with the 'No Es Hora De Callar' movement and joined its sixth symbolic return march of more than 500 survivors of sexual violence, was killed - the article calls it a trans feminicide - in Bolívar on 22 May, in Carmen de Bolívar; more than 19 days later the circumstances remained unclear, and friend and fellow social leader Yirley Velasco remembers her as having taken up the fight for trans rights in the municipality. The piece exposes the gap between official and NGO figures: the Fiscalía's own data base records 3,322 intentional homicides of people identified as LGBTIQ+ between January 2010 and May 2025, 431 for 2024 versus about 160 reported by the NGO (267 fewer), and 39 homicides in one Fiscalía dependency's 2025 data versus 156 in the policies-and-strategies base; experts cited describe the information system as neither unified nor reliable.
verdicts.note: region-specific source documenting the named killing (Nawar Jiménez, Carmen de Bolívar) and the figures-gap claims the record relies on
